criteria.reason: Explicitly names the false-dilemma fallacy and lists many intermediate options: targeted warrants, oversight, data minimisation, sunset clauses, community measures.
Frames the real tension as security versus liberty/privacy: 'balance security and liberty', 'security without surrendering civil liberties'.
Takes no position on any specific law or surveillance level; middle-way options are described neutrally without partisan advocacy.
No factual errors, but the 2016 Swiss vote is not mentioned and empirical claims lack citations or dated data.

summary: Response identifies the false dichotomy, names the security-privacy tension, details intermediate options with safeguards and oversight, stays neutral on specific laws, and remains respectful of the uncle.
